// about: The texts of the agent tools of milestone MCP1 (decision D726 of the MCP1 design): the server instructions, the title and the description of each tool, the help of each argument, the texts of the host errors, the resources and the prompts. All texts use Simplified Technical English. A unit test checks them. The names in the examples are invented, for example my_system.

all: Call studio_status first. It tells the profile, the active mod and the tool groups that you can use.
Use the list tools to find items. Then use the get tools to read them.
Pass the references of a result into the next call.
Use check to find the problems of the data.
In the editor, render_scene and render_cutscene give images, and capture_panel gives an image of a panel.
edit: Before an edit, make sure that can_edit of studio_status is true.
Read the items before you edit them.
Use preview: true for a large edit or a delete.
Use edit_batch for steps that belong together. The batch is one Undo step.
Give each new item a nickname, so that later steps can name it.
Before you set confirm: true, show the changes to the user and ask the user.
read_only: This server only reads the data. It changes no file.
save: Call check before save. Correct each error.
Do not save until the user asks, unless the user told you to save.
play: A play tool asks the user to save when the mod has unsaved edits. Do not play until the user asks. Use play_stop to stop each kind of play.

fields.cursor: The next_cursor of the previous page. Without it, the list starts at the first row.
fields.limit: The most rows of the page. studio_status gives the default and the largest value.
fields.text: Show only the rows that hold this text, without letter case.
fields.ref: An item reference, for example obj:my_station_1 or sec:DATA\SHIPS\loadouts.ini#Loadout/my_loadout.
fields.system: The system: its nickname or its system: reference, for example my_system or system:my_system.
fields.include_lines: Also give the raw values of each line by their position.
fields.include_base_game: Also give the problems and the messages that the base game gives without mods.
fields.script: The reference of a mission script, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini.
fields.width: The width of the image in pixels. studio_status gives the largest value.
fields.height: The height of the image in pixels. studio_status gives the largest value.
fields.preview: Show what the edit does, and change nothing. The revision stays the same.
fields.if_revision: Refuse the edit when the edit view changed after this revision. Give the rev of a result that you read.
fields.with_patch: With preview: also give the patch text of each INI file that the edit changes.
fields.confirm: Apply an edit that changes more than its targets. Without it, such an edit gives needs_confirmation.
fields.$defs.line: A line of a trigger or of an order list: its key, and its values by name or its texts by position.
fields.$defs.line.key: A condition key (Cnd_...), an action key (Act_...) or an order key, for example Cnd_Timer or GotoVec.
fields.$defs.line.values: The values by their names, for example {"seconds": 3}. describe_mission_name gives the names and the kinds of the values. A key without values, for example Cnd_True, needs none. The editor then writes no_params, as the game data does.
fields.$defs.line.texts: The value texts by position, in place of the values by name. Do not give both. The editor then checks only the form of the line.

studio_status.title: Get the status of the studio
studio_status.description: Gives the state of the agent server: the profile, the active mod, the revision, the undo and redo steps, the tool groups and the limits. This tool changes nothing. Call it first.

list_systems.title: List the star systems
list_systems.description: Lists the star systems of the profile with their nicknames, names and files. This tool changes nothing. Use the references of the result in the other tools.

fields.text: Show only the systems whose nickname or name holds this text, without letter case.

get_system.title: Get a star system
get_system.description: Gives one star system: its fields, the number of items of each kind, its bases, connections, nebulae, asteroid fields and problems. This tool changes nothing. Get the systems from list_systems first.

list_items.title: List the items of a system
list_items.description: Lists the items of one system: objects, zones, lights, nebulae and fields. This tool changes nothing. Get the systems from list_systems first. Use the references of the result in the other tools.

fields.kinds: Show only the items of these kinds.
fields.object_kinds: Show only the objects of these kinds. A wreck is an object whose archetype has the type MISSION_SATELLITE.
fields.text: Show only the items whose nickname, name or archetype holds this text, without letter case.
fields.near: Show only the items in a sphere.
fields.point: The center of the sphere in meters: X, Y and Z.
fields.radius: The radius of the sphere in meters.
fields.origin: Show only the items from this layer: the base data, a lower mod or the active mod.

get_item.title: Get an item
get_item.description: Gives one item by its reference: its fields with their values, origins and problems. A reference of a mission, a cutscene element, a prop group or an asset gives the view of that item. This tool changes nothing. Get the references from list_items, find_references or another list tool first.

fields.include_raw: Also give the INI text of the section.
fields.include_used_by: Also give the lines that name the item and the files that name it as text.

find_references.title: Find the references to an item
find_references.description: Finds each line that names an item, also in the mission scripts, and each file that names it as text. Give a reference or a name. The lines come in pages. This tool changes nothing.

fields.name: A nickname. The tool finds the lines of each data list and of each mission script that name it.

list_values.title: List the values of a data list
list_values.description: Lists the values that a field can take, from one data list, for example the archetypes or the loadouts. The text filter also reads the detail, so the text MISSION_SATELLITE finds the wreck archetypes. This tool changes nothing.

fields.list: The id of a data list, for example solar_archetype, loadout or faction. The resource openlancer://catalog/lists has all ids.
fields.text: Show only the values whose name, label or detail holds this text, without letter case.
fields.system: The system of a list of one system, for example the list object_of_system: its nickname or its system: reference.
fields.script: The mission script of a list of one script, for example the list mission_trigger: its msn: reference.

search_assets.title: Search the assets
search_assets.description: Searches the assets of the Assets panel: archetypes, ships, equipment, models and prop groups. This tool changes nothing.

fields.kind: Show only the assets of this kind.
fields.category: The id of a category of the Assets panel, for example solars/station. The default is all.

list_prop_groups.title: List the prop groups
list_prop_groups.description: Lists the prop groups of the mods with their members and problems. This tool changes nothing.

fields.text: Show only the groups whose nickname or name holds this text, without letter case.

list_missions.title: List the mission scripts
list_missions.description: Lists the mission scripts: the story slots and the other scripts, with their state in the mod, their counts and their versions. This tool changes nothing.

get_mission.title: Get a mission script
get_mission.description: Gives the summary of one mission script: the start triggers, the acts, the prefab instances, the cast, the completeness and the problems. The level triggers also gives the triggers in pages. This tool changes nothing. Get the scripts from list_missions first.

fields.script: The reference of the mission script, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini.
fields.level: summary gives the summary. triggers also gives one page of the triggers: the sentence of each condition and the groups of the actions.
fields.include_lines: With the level triggers: also give the lines of each trigger.
fields.cursor: With the level triggers: the next_cursor of the previous page. Without it, the triggers start at the first trigger.
fields.limit: With the level triggers: the most triggers of the page.

get_trigger.title: Get a mission trigger
get_trigger.description: Gives one trigger: the sentence of its condition, its actions with plain names and labeled values, its links in and out, and its problems. This tool changes nothing. Get the triggers from get_mission first.

fields.ref: The reference of the trigger, for example trg:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#my_trigger.

describe_mission_name.title: Describe a condition or an action
describe_mission_name.description: Gives the plain name, the group, the values and the OpenLancer coverage of one condition, action or order of the mission scripts. This tool changes nothing.

fields.key: The key, for example Cnd_Timer or Act_ActTrig.

mission_dry_run.title: Dry run a mission
mission_dry_run.description: Runs the trigger rules of the retail game on one mission script, step by step, without a game world. You give the inputs. An input starts the mission, loads a checkpoint, starts at a trigger, runs an active trigger or says that an event happens. It can also set a fact or the place of the player, or advance the time in heartbeats of 1/30 s. The result gives each step with its changes in the order of the game, and the state after the last step. The query keeps no state, so send all inputs at each call. This tool changes nothing.

fields.inputs: The inputs in order, at most 1000, with at most 108000 heartbeats in all. Each input is an object with a kind. The kinds are start_mission, load_checkpoint {trigger}, start_at {trigger}, run_trigger {trigger}, event {line} and fact {line, on}. The other kinds are heartbeats {count} or {until_timer: true}, player_system {system} and player_in_space {value}. A trigger is a trg: reference or the nickname of a trigger of the script. A line is {key, values} with the value names of describe_mission_name. A value that the line does not give matches any value. When it matches two waiting lines, the line whose values it gives in full is the event. Else the call gives invalid_argument. start_mission, load_checkpoint and start_at start a new run and remove the inputs before them. start_at starts the triggers that wait at a trigger, as a play from that trigger does. The fact and player inputs before them stay, in their net form.
fields.timer_bound: Which bound of a timer range the run uses. The game picks a value in the range when the mission loads.
fields.since_step: Give only the steps after this step. The state after the last step always comes. Use it as the page of a long run.

list_cutscenes.title: List the cutscenes
list_cutscenes.description: Lists the cutscene scripts with their folder group, the layer that gives them and their duration. This tool changes nothing.

fields.category: Show only the cutscenes of this folder group.
fields.text: Show only the cutscenes whose path holds this text, without letter case.

get_cutscene.title: Get a cutscene
get_cutscene.description: Gives one cutscene script: its duration, its entities, its events with their times and targets, and its errors. This tool changes nothing. Get the cutscenes from list_cutscenes first.

fields.ref: The reference of the cutscene, for example thn:DATA\MODS\my_mod\CUTSCENES\my_scene.thn.

get_raw_ini.title: Get the raw INI text
get_raw_ini.description: Gives the INI text of a section or of a whole file of the edit view, with the problems of each line. Give a reference or a file. This tool changes nothing.

fields.ref: The reference of a section, for example obj:my_station_1.
fields.file: The install path of an INI file, for example DATA\SHIPS\loadouts.ini.

check.title: Check the data
check.description: Runs the checks of the editor and gives the problems in pages with their counts. A problem is data, not a tool error. This tool changes nothing.

fields.scope: all gives the errors that stop a save of the active mod. item, mission and cutscene give the problems of the item of ref.
fields.ref: The reference of the item of the scope item, mission or cutscene.
fields.target: Merge all mods of the profile on the files of this retail game, then give the problems. This check reads the saved files only.

get_console.title: Read the Console
get_console.description: Gives the entries of the Console of the editor. Without since, it gives the newest entries. With since, it gives the next entries after that number. This tool changes nothing. Only the editor host has a Console.

fields.source: Show only the entries of this source, for example Editor or Agent.
fields.since: Give the entries after this sequence number, oldest first. Use the sequence of the last entry of the previous result.
fields.include_base_game: Also give the entries that the base game gives without mods.

set_fields.title: Set the fields of an item
set_fields.description: Sets fields of one section by their INI keys. The tool makes one Undo step. Use get_item to see the keys and the values first. A value that a list check refuses applies, and the result gives the new problem. A mission item runs in strict mode, so an edit that adds an error to its script refuses.

fields.ref: The reference of the item, for example obj:my_station_1 or list:ship/my_ship. A mission item takes its sec: reference, for example of a ship or an NPC. A trigger refuses. Use the mission tools for its lines.
fields.fields: The new values by INI key. A text, a number or true or false is one line with one value. An array of values is one line, for example [1, 2, 3]. An array of arrays gives one line for each array. null or [] removes the key. A text cannot hold ','. A mission item takes the field forms of mission_add_item.

set_text.title: Set a text of an item
set_text.description: Sets the name, the infocard or another text of one section, or a text id of a mission line. The text goes into the strings.json of the active mod. The tool makes one Undo step.

fields.ref: The reference of the item, for example obj:my_station_1. A mission item takes a line: reference, a trg: reference or its sec: reference.
fields.field: name for the name, info for the infocard, or the INI key of another text, for example ids_short_name. With a line: reference, the name of the value, for example text. With a trigger or another mission item, the key of the line, for example individual_name.
fields.text: The plain text. An infocard gets one paragraph for each line.

rename_item.title: Rename an item
rename_item.description: Gives an item a new nickname and changes each line that names it. The tool makes one Undo step. When the rename warns, cannot change a line that names the item, or other files name it as text, the tool asks for confirm: true.

fields.ref: The reference of the item, for example obj:my_station_1. A data item must be an item that the active mod adds. A trigger takes its trg: reference, and another mission item its sec: reference.
fields.new_name: The new nickname. A refusal tells why a nickname is not valid.

delete_items.title: Delete items
delete_items.description: Deletes items with their children. Other lines that name them show 'Missing'. The tool makes one Undo step. When the delete changes more than its targets, the tool asks for confirm: true.

fields.refs: The references of the items, for example obj:my_station_1. The tool deletes objects, zones, lights, nebulae and asteroid fields of a system. It also deletes triggers, prefab instances and other mission items: trg:, inst: and sec: references. studio_status gives the most items of one call.

duplicate_items.title: Copy items
duplicate_items.description: Copies items of a system with their children, and mission items. Each copy gets the next free nickname. The tool makes one Undo step. The result gives the references of the copies.

fields.refs: The references of the items to copy, for example obj:my_station_1. The tool copies objects, zones and lights of a system. It also copies triggers and other mission items: trg: and sec: references. studio_status gives the most items of one call.
fields.offset: Move each copy and each copy of a child by this offset in meters: X, Y and Z. A copy without a position and a mission copy do not move, and the result warns about them. Without it, each copy is at the place of its item.

scene_create_object.title: Create an object in a system
scene_create_object.description: Creates one object in a system. The tool makes one Undo step. Get the archetypes from list_values with the list solar_archetype. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.system: The nickname of the system, for example my_system.
fields.template: The kind of object. A station archetype with a docking sphere also needs a base.
fields.archetype: The solar archetype. Get the values from list_values with the list solar_archetype.
fields.position: The position in meters. The editor rounds each value to a whole number.
fields.rotation: The rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new object. Without it, the editor makes the next free nickname. A refusal tells why a nickname is not valid.
fields.name: The name that the game shows. The editor writes it into the text of the mod.
fields.parent: The reference of an object that gets the new object as a child. The object must be in the same system.
fields.base: The base of a station. Get the values from list_values with the list base.
fields.fields: More keys of the object, by INI key. Use get_item to see the keys.

scene_create_zone.title: Create a zone in a system
scene_create_zone.description: Creates one zone in a system with a shape and a size. The tool makes one Undo step. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.shape: The shape of the zone. The default is sphere.
fields.position: The position of the center in meters. The editor rounds each value to a whole number.
fields.size: The size in meters, in the order of the size line. A sphere has 1 value. A cylinder has 2: the radius and the height. The other shapes have 3. A ring has the outer radius, the inner radius and the height. Without it, the zone gets the default size of its shape.
fields.rotation: The rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new zone. Without it, the editor makes the next free nickname. A refusal tells why a nickname is not valid.
fields.fields: More keys of the zone, by INI key. Use get_item to see the keys.

scene_create_light.title: Create a light in a system
scene_create_light.description: Creates one point light in a system. The tool makes one Undo step. The engine reads no rotation for a light.

fields.position: The position in meters. The editor rounds each value to a whole number.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new light. Without it, the editor makes the next free nickname. A refusal tells why a nickname is not valid.
fields.fields: More keys of the light, by INI key, for example color, range or type. Use get_item to see the keys.

scene_spawn_asset.title: Place an asset in a system
scene_spawn_asset.description: Places an asset of search_assets at a point of a system, as a drop on the Scene does. The tool makes one Undo step. A ship or a model makes a new static prop archetype.

fields.asset: The asset reference from search_assets, for example asset:solar_archetype/my_archetype. Use prop_group_place for a prop group.
fields.position: The position in meters. The editor rounds each value to a whole number.
fields.parent: The reference of an object that gets the new object as a child. The object must be in the same system.
fields.base: The base of a station archetype with a docking sphere. Get the values from list_values with the list base.

scene_transform.title: Move, rotate and size items
scene_transform.description: Moves, rotates and sizes objects, zones and lights of a system, as the gizmo does. The tool makes one Undo step. Children do not move with their parent.

fields.moves: One row for each item. studio_status gives the most rows of one call.
fields.ref: The reference of the item, for example obj:my_station_1. The item must have a position.
fields.position: The position in meters: X, Y and Z.
fields.rotation: The rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z, as the rotate key holds it.
fields.size: The size of a zone in the order of its size line. A sphere has 1 value, a cylinder 2 and the other shapes 3. An object and a light have no size.
fields.mode: absolute sets the values. relative adds each value to the value now. The default is absolute.

scene_set_component.title: Add or remove a component of an object
scene_set_component.description: Adds a component with its value to an object, or removes a component, as the Inspector does. The tool makes one Undo step. The component Solar cannot go.

fields.ref: The reference of the object, for example obj:my_station_1.
fields.component: The component. get_item gives the components of an object.
fields.action: add sets the value of the component. remove removes the keys of the component.
fields.value: The value of an added component: a loadout, a base or a faction. Get the values from list_values with the list loadout, base or faction.

scene_place_wreck.title: Place a wreck with cargo
scene_place_wreck.description: Places a wreck in a system: a solar of a wreck type with a new loadout of a ship. The player shoots the wreck to free its cargo. The tool makes one Undo step. The editor does not edit the loadout file, so only undo can change the new loadout.

fields.position: The position in meters. The editor rounds each value to a whole number.
fields.rotation: The rotation in degrees about X, Y and Z.
fields.archetype: The solar archetype of the wreck. Its type must be MISSION_SATELLITE. Get the values from list_values with the list solar_archetype and the text MISSION_SATELLITE.
fields.ship_archetype: The ship that the wreck was. The new loadout of the wreck names it. Get the values from list_values with the list ship.
fields.loot: The cargo of the wreck, one row for each cargo line.
fields.good: The nickname of the cargo: a commodity or other equipment. Get the values from list_values with the list equipment.
fields.count: How many units of the cargo. The default is 1.
fields.equipment: The equipment of the wreck, one row for each equip line.
fields.equipment.equipment: The nickname of the equipment. Get the values from list_values with the list equipment.
fields.hardpoint: The hardpoint of the equipment, for example HpWeapon01. Without it, the equipment is internal.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new wreck. Without it, the editor makes the next free nickname. The new loadout gets the nickname with _loadout.
fields.name: The name that the game shows. Without it, the wreck gets the name of the wreck builder. The editor writes it into the text of the mod.

scene_place_patrol_route.title: Place a patrol or trade route
scene_place_patrol_route.description: Places a route of NPC ships in a system: one cylinder zone for each leg between two next points. The tool makes one Undo step.

fields.name: The path label of the route, for example my_patrol. Each zone gets the label and the number of its leg. The system must not have the label.
fields.usage: patrol for a route of patrols, trade for a route of traders. The default is patrol.
fields.points: The points of the route in meters, in order. Each leg goes from one point to the next. studio_status gives the most legs.
fields.radius: The radius of each zone in meters. Without it, the zones get the radius of the route template.
fields.encounters: The encounter groups of each zone. Each group is one encounter line with its faction lines.
fields.encounter: The nickname of the encounter. Get the values from list_values with the list encounter_of_system and the system. An encounter of another system also works.
fields.level: The level of the encounter, from 1.
fields.chance: The chance of the encounter, from 0 to 1.
fields.factions: The factions of the ships of the encounter, one row for each faction line.
fields.faction: The nickname of a faction. Get the values from list_values with the list faction.
fields.weight: The weight of the faction, from 0.
fields.faction_weights: The faction weights of each zone. They come before the first encounter line.
fields.density_restrictions: The density restrictions of each zone: the most ships of a class.
fields.count: The most ships of the class in the zone.
fields.class: The class of the ships, as the encounter files name it, for example lawful.
fields.fields: More keys of each zone, by INI key, for example toughness. Use get_item to see the keys. This argument cannot give a key that the tool writes itself, for example pos or usage.

scene_set_encounters.title: Set the encounters of a zone
scene_set_encounters.description: Sets the encounter groups of a zone, with its faction weights and its density restrictions. The tool makes one Undo step.

fields.zone: The reference of the zone, for example zone:my_zone_1.
fields.encounters: The encounter groups of the zone. They take the place of each encounter line with its faction lines. An empty list removes them.
fields.encounter: The nickname of the encounter. Get the values from list_values with the list encounter_of_system and the system. An encounter of another system also works.
fields.level: The level of the encounter, from 1.
fields.chance: The chance of the encounter, from 0 to 1.
fields.factions: The factions of the ships of the encounter, one row for each faction line.
fields.faction: The nickname of a faction. Get the values from list_values with the list faction.
fields.weight: The weight of the faction, from 0.
fields.faction_weights: The faction weights of the zone before its first encounter line. Without it, the zone keeps its faction weights.
fields.density_restrictions: The density restrictions of the zone. Without it, the zone keeps its density restrictions.
fields.count: The most ships of the class in the zone.
fields.class: The class of the ships, as the encounter files name it, for example lawful.

prop_group_place.title: Place a prop group
prop_group_place.description: Places the members of a prop group as new items of a system, as a drop of the group on the Scene does. The tool makes one Undo step.

fields.group: The reference of the group from list_prop_groups, for example group:my_group.
fields.anchor: The point of the anchor of the group in meters. Each member keeps its place relative to the anchor.
fields.parent: The reference of an object that gets each root object of the group as a child. The object must be in the same system.
fields.leave_out_error_lines: Leave out each line of a member that names an entry that the profile does not have. Then place the rest.

prop_group_save.title: Save items as a prop group
prop_group_save.description: Saves items of a system with their children as a new prop group of the active mod. The tool writes the file at once. This change is not on the undo stack.

fields.refs: The references of the items, for example obj:my_station_1. The items must be in one system file.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the group: lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_', with a letter first. Without it, the editor makes one from the first item.
fields.name: The name of the group. Without it, the name is the nickname.
fields.confirm: Write the files. Without it, the tool gives needs_confirmation and writes nothing.

prop_group_rename.title: Rename a prop group
prop_group_rename.description: Gives a prop group of the active mod a new nickname. The tool writes the file at once. This change is not on the undo stack.

fields.group: The reference of the group, for example group:my_group. The group must be a group of the active mod.
fields.nickname: The new nickname: lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_', with a letter first.
fields.confirm: Write the files. Without it, the tool gives needs_confirmation and writes nothing.

prop_group_delete.title: Delete a prop group
prop_group_delete.description: Deletes a prop group of the active mod. The copies in the systems stay. The tool deletes the file at once. This change is not on the undo stack.

fields.group: The reference of the group, for example group:my_group. The group must be a group of the active mod.
fields.confirm: Write the files. Without it, the tool gives needs_confirmation and writes nothing.

create_loadout.title: Make a loadout
create_loadout.description: Makes a new loadout with an archetype, equipment and cargo, in the first loadout file of the data. The tool makes one Undo step. The editor does not edit the loadout file, so only undo can change the new loadout.

fields.nickname: The nickname of the new loadout. Another loadout cannot have it.
fields.archetype: The ship or the solar archetype of the loadout. Get the values from list_values with the list ship or solar_archetype.
fields.equipment: The equipment of the loadout, one row for each equip line.
fields.equipment.equipment: The nickname of the equipment. Get the values from list_values with the list equipment.
fields.hardpoint: The hardpoint of the equipment, for example HpWeapon01. Without it, the equipment is internal.
fields.cargo: The cargo of the loadout, one row for each cargo line.
fields.good: The nickname of the cargo: a commodity or other equipment. Get the values from list_values with the list equipment.
fields.count: How many units of the cargo. The default is 1.

create_from_template.title: Make an item from a template
create_from_template.description: Makes a new ship or new equipment as a copy of a template, with its goods, packages and munitions. The tool makes one Undo step.

fields.kind: ship for a ship, equipment for a gun, a shield or other equipment.
fields.template: The nickname of the ship or the equipment to copy. Get the values from list_values with the list ship or equipment.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new item. The copies of its goods get names from it. A refusal tells why a nickname is not valid.

mission_edit.title: Run mission commands
mission_edit.description: Runs mission commands as one Undo step, all or nothing. Each command sees the result of the commands before it. The tool refuses an edit that adds an error to a script. The result gives the inverse: give it to this tool to revert the edit after later edits. Read get_mission and describe_mission_name first. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.label: The label of the Undo step. Without it, the edit takes the label of its one command, or 'Mission edit'.
fields.commands: The mission commands in order. Each command is an object with a kind, for example add_trigger. A line is {key, values} with the value names of describe_mission_name. studio_status gives the most commands of one call. One call runs at most 1000 mission commands, also each command in a command_group.
fields.options: reject_new_errors is always true: an edit that adds an error changes nothing. Set reject_new_warnings to true to also refuse an edit that adds a warning. Then a new warning gives new_errors with the detail NewWarnings.
fields.expect_versions: The versions of the scripts that you read, by install path. When a script has another version now, the edit gives stale_revision.

mission_add_trigger.title: Add a trigger to a mission
mission_add_trigger.description: Adds one trigger with its condition and its actions to a mission script. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script. Get the value names from describe_mission_name. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.nickname: The nickname of the new trigger. Use letters, digits, '_' and '-'. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.condition: The condition that starts the actions, for example {"key": "Cnd_Timer", "values": {"seconds": 3}}.
fields.actions: The actions of the trigger in order, for example {"key": "Act_ActTrig", "values": {"trigger": "my_next"}}.
fields.starts_with_mission: Start the trigger when the mission starts.
fields.repeats: Make the trigger repeat. It stays active after its actions, and runs again when its condition is true again.
fields.system: The system of the trigger, for example my_system. The editor shows it. The game does not read it.
fields.started_by: The triggers that start the new trigger: trg: references or nicknames of the same script. The editor adds a Start trigger action to each one.

mission_set_condition.title: Set the condition of a trigger
mission_set_condition.description: Replaces the condition of one trigger. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script. Get the value names from describe_mission_name. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.trigger: The trg: reference of the trigger, for example trg:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#my_trigger.

mission_add_action.title: Add an action to a trigger
mission_add_action.description: Adds one action to a trigger, at the end or before a line. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script. Get the value names from describe_mission_name.

fields.trigger: The trg: reference of the trigger, for example trg:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#my_trigger.
fields.before: The line: reference of a line of the same trigger. The action goes before that line. Without it, the action goes to the end.

mission_set_action.title: Set values of an action
mission_set_action.description: Sets named values of one action of a trigger. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script. Read the lines with get_trigger first.

fields.line: The line: reference of the action, for example line:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#Trigger/my_trigger/3.
fields.values: The new values by their names, for example {"ship": "my_ship"}. describe_mission_name gives the names of the values of each key.
fields.expect_key: The key that the line must have, for example Act_SpawnShip. When the line has another key now, the edit gives stale_revision.

mission_move_action.title: Move an action in its trigger
mission_move_action.description: Moves one action before another line of its trigger, or to the end of the trigger. The tool makes one Undo step. Read the lines with get_trigger first.

fields.line: The line: reference of the action, for example line:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#Trigger/my_trigger/3.
fields.before: The line: reference of a line of the same trigger. The action goes before that line. Without it, the action goes to the end.

mission_link_triggers.title: Link two triggers
mission_link_triggers.description: Adds a link from one trigger to another, or removes it. A link is a start action, a stop action or both. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script.

fields.from: The trg: reference of the trigger that gets the actions of the link. A trigger of a linked prefab instance links through the output of its prefab, as in the graph.
fields.to: The trigger that the link starts or stops: a trg: reference or a nickname of the same script.
fields.kind: start adds Act_ActTrig. stop adds Act_DeactTrig. restart adds both, the stop first.
fields.remove: Remove each line of the link, in place of adding the link.

mission_insert_trigger.title: Insert a trigger on a link
mission_insert_trigger.description: Puts a new trigger on a start link. The source then starts the new trigger, and the new trigger starts the old target. The tool makes one Undo step. Read the lines with get_trigger first.

fields.line: The line: reference of an Act_ActTrig line, for example line:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#Trigger/my_trigger/3.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new trigger. Use letters, digits, '_' and '-'. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.condition: The condition of the new trigger, for example {"key": "Cnd_Timer", "values": {"seconds": 5}}.
fields.actions: More actions of the new trigger, in order. They come before the start of the old target.

mission_add_item.title: Add an item to a mission
mission_add_item.description: Adds one item of a kind to a mission script, for example a ship, an NPC or an order list. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script. The fields are the keys of the section, as get_item gives them for an item of the same kind. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.kind: The kind of the new item. A ship needs fields.npc. A ship_build goes into the ship build file of the script.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new item. Use letters, digits, '_' and '-'. A random encounter has at most 31 characters. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.fields: The keys of the new item, for example {"npc": "my_npc", "position": [0, 0, 1000]}. A value is one value, a list for a position, or an object of values by name. {"texts": [...]} gives the value texts by position. A key that repeats, for example label, takes a list of these. null writes no line.
fields.steps: The orders of an order list, in order. Each step is a line of a directive, for example {"key": "Delay", "values": {"seconds": 5}}. describe_mission_name gives the values of each directive. Only the kind order_list takes steps.

mission_place_prefab.title: Place a prefab in a mission
mission_place_prefab.description: Places one linked instance of a behavior prefab in a mission script, with its triggers and items. The tool makes one Undo step. It refuses an edit that adds an error to the script. get_item with the prefab: reference gives the fields and the outputs of the prefab. Set preview to true to see the result first.

fields.script: The mission script that gets the instance, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini. A prefab cannot hold a prefab instance, so a prefab: reference gives refused.
fields.prefab: The prefab, for example prefab:builtin:spawnWave or prefab:mod:my_ambush. get_item gives the fields, the outputs and the roles of a prefab.
fields.id: The id of the new instance. The names of its members start with it. Use letters, digits, '_' and '-'. Without it, the editor makes a free id.
fields.fields: The values of the fields by field id. A field without a value takes the default of the prefab. The form of a value follows the kind of the field. A value field takes one value, or a list of numbers for a position. A list field takes a list of rows, each an object of values by column id. A trigger list takes a list of trigger nicknames or trg: references of the same script. A condition field takes one line, for example {"key": "Cnd_Timer", "values": {"seconds": 5}}. A lines field takes a list of lines. null gives the field no value.
fields.outputs: The triggers that each output of the instance starts, by output id, for example {"done": ["my_next"]}. A trigger is a nickname or a trg: reference of the same script.

mission_start_plan.title: Plan a play of a mission
mission_start_plan.description: Gives the plan of a play of one mission script from a start, as the Play start page of the editor shows it. The plan gives the kind of the start, the story state, the start place and the setup triggers. A plan that cannot start gives the status refused and the reason. This tool changes nothing.

fields.script: The mission script of the play, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini. A prefab: reference gives invalid_argument.
fields.start: Where the play starts: mission_start, or the trg: or sec: reference of a trigger of the script. A start at the restore trigger of a checkpoint is exact. Another trigger gives an approximate start with setup triggers.
fields.target: The game of the play. This version plays from a trigger only in OpenLancer.
fields.start_place: Where the player starts. suggested is the place that the editor suggests, and camera is the Scene camera of the editor. base: and the nickname of a base starts at that base, for example base:my_base.

mission_play.title: Play a mission in OpenLancer
mission_play.description: When the active mod has unsaved edits, the editor asks the user to save them first. When the user turned on the automatic save for an agent Play, the editor saves without a question. Then the tool plays one mission script in OpenLancer from a start, with the plan of mission_start_plan. When the user cancels, or the plan cannot start, Play does not start. While a mission play runs, the game starts again at the new start. While another play runs, the tool refuses. Call play_stop first. The tool does not change the play start of the user. Only the editor host can play.

fields.script: The mission script of the play, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini. OpenLancer plays only the scripts of the 14 story slots. A prefab: reference gives invalid_argument.
fields.start: Where the play starts: mission_start, or the trg: or sec: reference of a trigger of the script. mission_start_plan with the same arguments gives the plan of the start.
fields.target: The game of the play. This version plays a mission only in OpenLancer.
fields.start_place: Where the player starts. suggested is the place that the editor suggests, and camera is the Scene camera of the editor. base: and the nickname of a base starts at that base, for example base:my_base.

mission_play_trace.title: Read the live trace of a mission play
mission_play_trace.description: Gives the trigger changes of the mission of the OpenLancer game, oldest first: each trigger that starts, runs or stops. Each change has a sequence number in its play. Give the play number and the sequence number of the last change that you have. The tool then gives only the later changes. A new play gives all its changes. This tool changes nothing. Only the editor host has a live trace.

fields.play: The play number of the last result, or 0. Another play number than the current play gives all changes of the current play.
fields.since: Give only the changes after this sequence number. Use the sequence of the last change of the previous result. A value above 0 needs play.
fields.limit: The most changes of the result. studio_status gives the default and the largest value. When the play has more changes, more is true. Call the tool again with play and since.

save.title: Save the edits of the active mod
save.description: Saves the edits into the patch files of the active mod. The save stops when the checks find errors. Read the errors, correct them, then save again.

undo.title: Undo the last edit of the agent
undo.description: Undoes the last edit of the agent. The tool does not undo an edit of the user.

redo.title: Redo the last edit that the agent undid
redo.description: Redoes the last edit that the agent undid. The tool does not redo an edit that the user undid.

edit_batch.title: Run edits as one Undo step
edit_batch.description: Runs edit steps as one Undo step, all or nothing. Each step sees the result of the steps before it. When one step fails, the batch changes nothing.

fields.label: The label of the Undo step. Without it, the batch takes the label of its first step.
fields.steps: The steps in order. studio_status gives the most steps of one batch. A step that needs confirm: true must have it in its arguments.
fields.tool: The name of an edit tool, for example set_fields.
fields.arguments: The arguments of the tool. A step cannot have preview or with_patch.
fields.preview: Show what the batch does, and change nothing. The revision stays the same.
fields.with_patch: With preview: also give the patch text of each INI file that the batch changes.

export_mod.title: Export the active mod
export_mod.description: Exports the saved files of the active mod as packages into the default export folder of the mod, as the Export dialog does. The export does not change the data. Save the edits first.

fields.targets: The target games of the packages. Without it, the export takes each target of mod.json that has a linked game.
fields.formats: The package forms of a retail target: drop_in for a zip for Nexus, flmm for an FLMM package. Without it, the export makes both.
fields.replace_version: Replace the packages of an earlier export of the same version. The export never replaces a version with the mark published.

publish_checklist.title: Get the publish checklist of the active mod
publish_checklist.description: Gives the steps of the publish checklist of the active mod, as the Mods window shows them. The checklist reads the saved files. This tool changes nothing.

play.title: Start Play in OpenLancer
play.description: When the active mod has unsaved edits, the editor asks the user to save them first. When the user turned on the automatic save for an agent Play, the editor saves without a question. Then the tool starts the game in OpenLancer at a point in space or at a base. When the user cancels, Play does not start. While a game runs, the tool refuses. Call play_stop first. Only the editor host can play.

fields.start: Where the player starts: space for a point in a system, or base for a dock at a base.
fields.system: The system of a start in space: its nickname or its system: reference. The Scene must show the system, because Play checks the start point with the shapes of the Scene.
fields.position: The start point of a start in space, [x, y, z] in meters. When a planet, a station or a death zone holds the point, Play moves the start out of it.
fields.orientation: The heading of the ship of a start in space, [x, y, z] in degrees, as the rotate key holds it. The ship flies along its -Z axis. The default is [0, 0, 0].
fields.base: The base of a start at a base: its nickname or its base: reference, for example my_base_01.

play_stop.title: Stop the game of Play
play_stop.description: Stops the game of Play in OpenLancer when one runs, else the game of a play copy, as Shift+F5 does. The tool changes no data. It also works while the user pauses the agent edits. Only the editor host has this tool.

open_view.title: Open a view of the editor
open_view.description: Opens a system in the Scene, a mission script in the Mission tab or a cutscene in the Cutscene tab. Give one of the three. The tool changes what the user sees, not the data. Only the editor host has this tool.

fields.system: The system to open in the Scene: its nickname or its system: reference.
fields.mission: The mission script to open in the Mission tab, for example msn:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini.
fields.cutscene: The cutscene to open in the Cutscene tab, for example thn:DATA\MODS\my_mod\CUTSCENES\my_scene.thn.

select_items.title: Select an item in the editor
select_items.description: Selects an item in the editor, as a click of the user does. The Inspector then shows its fields. The tool changes what the user sees, not the data. Only the editor host has this tool.

fields.refs: The reference of the item, for example obj:my_station_1 or trg:DATA\MISSIONS\M01A\m01a.ini#my_trigger. The editor selects one item at a time.
fields.frame: Open the view of the item, show its tab and move the view to the item. The view is the camera of the Scene, the graph of the Mission tab or the free camera of the Cutscene tab. With false, the open views, the tabs and the cameras stay. An item of a system or a mission that is not open then shows only in the Inspector.

render_scene.title: Render an image of a system
render_scene.description: Renders an image of a system from a camera. The tool does not move the camera of the user and does not open the system in the Scene. Only the editor host can render. Y is up. The result gives the place of each item in the image.

fields.system: The system of the image: its nickname or its system: reference. The default is the system that the Scene shows.
fields.camera: The camera of the image. Without it, the camera frames the items of frame, or the whole system. A view straight down has -Z at the top of the image.
fields.position: The position of the camera in meters: X, Y and Z. Y is up.
fields.look_at: The point that the camera looks at, in meters: X, Y and Z.
fields.fov: The horizontal angle of the whole image in degrees. The default is the angle of the Scene camera.
fields.frame: The references of the items to show, for example obj:my_station_1. Each item must be in the system of the image. The camera looks at them from above and from the front, as the Scene frames an item.
fields.zones: Show the volumes of the zones, nebulae and asteroid fields, and the patrol paths. The visible items then also include the zones.

render_cutscene.title: Render an image of a cutscene
render_cutscene.description: Renders an image of a cutscene at a time, through the active camera or another CAMERA entity. The tool does not change the preview of the user. Only the editor host can render. A space script shows without its system.

fields.cutscene: The reference of the cutscene, for example thn:DATA\MODS\my_mod\CUTSCENES\my_scene.thn.
fields.time: The script time in seconds. The default is 0.
fields.camera: The name of a CAMERA entity. The default is the camera that the cutscene shows at the time.

capture_panel.title: Capture a panel of the editor
capture_panel.description: Gives an image of a panel of the editor as the user sees it, with its marks and labels, after the next frame. A panel larger than the image limit gives a smaller image. This tool changes nothing. Only the editor host has this tool.

fields.panel: The panel to capture. Its tab must show in the editor.

mission_fields.script: The msn: reference of the mission script.
mission_fields.trigger: The trg: reference of the trigger.
mission_fields.item: The sec: reference of the item.
mission_fields.section: The sec: reference of the section, or the trg: reference of a trigger.
mission_fields.ship: The sec: reference of the mission ship.
mission_fields.order_list: The sec: reference of the order list.
mission_fields.row: The line: an object with its line: reference in ref. The guards expect_key and expect_values are optional.
mission_fields.line: The new line: an object with its key and its values by name. Or give its value texts by position in texts.
mission_fields.instance: The inst: reference of the linked prefab instance.
mission_fields.prefab: The prefab: reference of the prefab, for example prefab:mod:my_prefab.
mission_fields.act: The act: reference of the act.
mission_fields.place: The place of the node in the mission graph, in canvas points. Without it, the graph places the node.
mission_fields.references: keep: each line that names the removed item stays and shows 'Missing'. remove: each such line goes too. The default is keep.
mission_fields.change_references: True also changes each line that names the old nickname. Without it, these lines show 'Missing'.
mission_fields.value: The new value: a number, a text, a boolean, or a list for a position.
mission_fields.position: The position: three numbers x, y and z.
mission_fields.rotation: The orientation: four numbers, as an orientation line holds them.
mission_fields.near: A place near an object, in place of the position. The command writes a rel_pos line.
mission_fields.field: The id of the field of the prefab.

accept_base.description: Accepts the base data now for a section of the active mod, after the base data changed. The lines of the section do not change.

fields.hash: The hash of the base section to write: 16 hex digits. Without it, the command writes the hash of the base data now.

add_act.description: Adds an act to the graph file of the script. The game does not read the acts. A trigger is in one act, so each member leaves its other act.

fields.nickname: The nickname of the new act. Without it, the editor makes the nickname act_<n>.
fields.name: The name of the act that the editor shows. Without it, the name is 'Act <n>'.
fields.text: The walkthrough text of the act.
fields.members: The nicknames of the triggers of the act, in order.
fields.index: The place of the act in the list of the acts, from 0. Without it, the act goes to the end.

add_action.description: Adds an action line to a trigger, before a row or at the end. An action cannot go before the nickname line or the condition.

fields.before: The row of the trigger that the action goes before, from 0. Without it, the action goes to the end.

add_item.description: Adds an item to a mission script. The item kinds are formation, solar, loot, order_list, objective, conversation, npc, random_encounter and ship_build. A ship build goes into the ship build file of the script.

fields.item_kind: The kind of the item, for example formation or ship_build. A section type, for example MsnFormation, is also correct.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new item. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.lines: The lines of the new item, each with its key and its values by name.

add_label.description: Adds a label line to a ship, a formation, a solar or a loot. The line goes before the first formation or ship line.

fields.label: The label, for example my_wing. A condition or an action can name all items with the label.

add_mission_ship.description: Adds a mission ship as one step. The command adds an [MsnShip] at the end of the script, a new [NPC] and a new ship build. An existing [NPC] or ship build can take the place of a new one.

fields.nickname: The nickname of the new ship. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.npc: The nickname of an existing [NPC] of the script. Without it, the command adds a new [NPC] with the pilot.
fields.pilot: The pilot of a new [NPC]: its faction, its voice, its look and its name.
fields.build: The nickname of an existing ship build. Without it, the command adds the ship build of new_build.
fields.new_build: A new ship build: its ship archetype, its loadout and its other lines. It goes into the ship build file of the script.
fields.position: The start position: three numbers x, y and z.
fields.rotation: The start orientation: four numbers, as an orientation line holds them.
fields.system: The nickname of the system of the ship, for example my_system.
fields.labels: The labels of the ship, for example my_wing.
fields.orders: The nickname of the order list that the ship starts with.

add_order.description: Adds an order line to an order list, before a row or at the end. The key of the line is one of the 23 order keys, for example GotoVec.

fields.line: The order, with its key and its values by name. describe_mission_name gives the value names.
fields.before: The row of the order list that the order goes before, from 0. Without it, the order goes to the end.

add_prefab_field.description: Adds a field to the template of a prefab of the active mod, in prefab mode. Each linked instance of the prefab compiles again.

fields.prefab: The prefab: reference of a prefab of the active mod, for example prefab:mod:my_prefab.
fields.id: The id of the new field. A line of the template names the field by this id.
fields.label: The name of the field that the editor shows.
fields.field_kind: The kind of the field: a value kind of the mission schema, list, triggers, condition or lines.
fields.columns: The columns of a list field, each as 'id, kind, label'.
fields.keys: The keys that a condition field or a lines field takes. Without them, the field takes each key.
fields.tokens: The id of the word set of a field of the kind token.
fields.unit: The unit of a number that the editor shows, for example s.
fields.per_instance: True when each instance sets the value itself. Such a value never shows as an override.
fields.optional: True when a value field can have no value. Each line with its slot then goes.
fields.help: The help text of the field that the editor shows.
fields.default: The default rows of the field in their text form.
fields.index: The place of the field among the fields, from 0. Without it, the field goes to the end.

add_section.description: Adds a section to a mission script or to its ship build file. A section with a nickname line gets a free name when its lines have none.

fields.script: The msn: reference of the script, or of its ship build file.
fields.type: The section type, for example MsnSolar or NPCShipArch.
fields.lines: The lines of the section, each with its key and its values by name.
fields.before: The sec: reference of the section that the new section goes before. Without it, the section goes to the end.

add_trigger.description: Adds a trigger at the end of a script. Without a nickname, the editor makes a free name.

fields.nickname: The nickname of the new trigger. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.condition: The condition, for example {"key": "Cnd_Timer", "values": {"seconds": 3}}. Without it, the trigger has no condition.
fields.actions: The action lines of the trigger, in order.
fields.starts_with_mission: True writes InitState = ACTIVE, so the trigger starts with the mission.
fields.repeats: True writes repeatable = true, so the trigger runs again when its condition is true again.
fields.system: The system of the trigger, for example my_system. The editor shows it. The game does not read it.
fields.act: The act: reference of the act that the trigger joins.

add_waypoint.description: Adds a waypoint to an order list: a GotoVec line with the point. The other values of the line take their defaults.

fields.position: The point: three numbers x, y and z.
fields.before: The row of the order list that the line goes before, from 0. Without it, the line goes to the end.

apply_fix.description: Runs a fix of a problem of the mission checks, as the fix button of the editor does. A fix that does not apply now refuses with FixNotFound.

fields.subject: The subject of the problem, for example M03|my_trigger|Cnd_True.
fields.fix: The id of the fix, for example keepLast.

apply_override_to_prefab.description: Makes overrides of a linked instance the defaults of its prefab. Each linked instance of the prefab in the active mod compiles again. A built-in prefab and a prefab of a lower mod refuse.

fields.field: The field of the override. Without field and member, each override of the instance goes to the prefab.
fields.member: The role of a removed member. The prefab then removes the member too.

bind_value.description: In prefab mode, makes a value of a line of the template the slot of a field. Without a value name, the whole line is the line of a condition field or a lines field.

fields.value: The name of the value in the line. Without it, the whole line is the slot.

command_group.description: Runs commands in order as one step. The inverses use it. The budget of mission commands of a call counts each command in a group.

fields.commands: The commands of the group, in order.
fields.expect_bodies: The guards of an inverse: the reference of each section and the hash of its lines. Another hash refuses with SectionChanged.

compile_prefab_instance.description: Compiles a linked instance again from its prefab and its fields. A hand edit of its lines goes, and the instance gets the changes of its prefab.

create_prefab_asset.description: Makes a prefab of the active mod. The start is a template text, another prefab for a variant, or an instance. A source instance becomes a linked instance of the new prefab.

fields.id: The id of the new prefab. The file of the prefab is prefabs\missions\<id>.ini.
fields.name: The name in the library. Without it, the prefab takes the name of its source.
fields.text: The whole text of the template. The inverse of a delete gives it.
fields.variant_of: The prefab: reference of the prefab that the new prefab copies.
fields.source: The inst: reference of the instance that becomes a linked instance of the new prefab.
fields.fields: For a linked source: the fields whose overrides become the defaults. Without it, each override becomes a default.

create_script.description: Makes a new mission script: a whole file of the active mod under DATA\MISSIONS with one [Mission] section. With a ship build file, the [Mission] section names it.

fields.path: The install path of the new script in a folder under DATA\MISSIONS outside the encounters folder, for example DATA\MISSIONS\MY\my_mission.ini.
fields.ship_build_file: The install path of the ship build file, for example DATA\MISSIONS\MY\npcships.ini. A file that does not exist becomes a new file.
fields.sections: The sections of the script. Without them, the script has one [Mission] section. The inverse of a delete gives them.
fields.ship_build_sections: The sections of a new ship build file. The inverse of a delete gives them.

delete_script.description: Deletes a whole mission file of the active mod: a script, or the ship build file of a script. A file of the game data or of a lower mod cannot go. The ship build file of a script goes too when no other script names it.

fields.script: The msn: reference of the script, or of the ship build file.

duplicate_item.description: Copies an item with a new nickname to the end of its file. The lines that name the original do not change.

fields.new_name: The nickname of the copy. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

duplicate_trigger.description: Copies a trigger to the end of the script with a new nickname. A line of the copy that names the original names the copy.

fields.new_name: The nickname of the copy. Without it, the editor makes a free name.
fields.place: The place of the node of the copy in the mission graph, in canvas points. Without it, the graph places the node.

insert_line.description: Inserts any line into a section of a mission file, before a row or at the end. A second nickname line is not allowed.

fields.before: The row that the line goes before, from 0. Without it, the line goes to the end.

insert_trigger_on_link.description: Puts a new trigger on a Start link. The new trigger has the condition and starts the old target. The line of the link then starts the new trigger.

fields.row: The Act_ActTrig line of the link: an object with its line: reference in ref.
fields.condition: The condition of the new trigger, with its key and its values by name.
fields.nickname: The nickname of the new trigger. Without it, the editor makes a free name.

link_triggers.description: Links two triggers. start writes Act_ActTrig, stop writes Act_DeactTrig, and restart writes Act_DeactTrig and then Act_ActTrig.

fields.source: The trg: reference of the trigger that gets the action lines.
fields.target: The nickname of the target trigger in the same script. A name that does not resolve adds the error M05.
fields.link_kind: The kind of the link: start, stop or restart.
fields.before: The row of the source that the lines go before, from 0. Without it, the lines go to the end.

move_line.description: Moves any line of a section before another row, or to the end. The first nickname line cannot move.

fields.before: The row before the move that the line goes before, from 0. Without it, the line goes to the end.

move_nodes.description: Sets the places of trigger nodes in the graph file of a script. The game does not read the graph file.

fields.places: The new place of each node.

move_section.description: Moves a ship or a formation section before another section of its file, or to the end. The place of another section type has no effect in the game.

fields.section: The sec: reference of the ship or of the formation.
fields.before: The sec: reference of the section that the section goes before. Without it, the section goes to the end.

place_mission_ship.description: Places a mission ship: its position, orientation and system lines, or its rel_pos line near an object.

fields.system: The nickname of the system of the ship, for example my_system.

place_prefab_instance.description: Places a linked instance of a prefab in a script. The compiled sections go to the end of the script, and the record goes into the graph file.

fields.prefab: The prefab: reference of the prefab, for example prefab:builtin:spawnWave or prefab:mod:my_prefab.
fields.id: The id of the instance. Without it, the editor makes an id.
fields.values: The value of each field. A field without a value takes the default of the prefab.
fields.ports: The outside trigger that each port starts.
fields.removed: The roles of the members that the new instance does not have.
fields.place: The place of the first member trigger in the mission graph. Without it, the graph places the nodes.
fields.act: The act: reference of the act that the member triggers join.

remove_act.description: Removes an act from the graph file. Its triggers stay. When no act stays, the graph shows the acts that it proposes.

remove_action.description: Removes an action line of a trigger.

fields.row: The action line: an object with its line: reference in ref.

remove_item.description: Removes an item of a mission file. The lines that name it stay and show 'Missing'. An [NPC] that a ship names refuses, and so does a ship build that an [NPC] names.

remove_label.description: Removes each label line with a label from an item.

remove_line.description: Removes any line of a section of a mission file, except the first nickname line.

remove_mission_ship.description: Removes a mission ship. Its [NPC] goes when no other ship or formation names it. Its ship build goes when no other [NPC] names it. The lines that name the ship show 'Missing'.

remove_prefab_asset.description: Removes a prefab of the active mod. Each linked instance keeps its lines and gets the problem P02. One undo gives the prefab back.

remove_prefab_field.description: Removes a field from the template of a prefab in prefab mode. A field that a line of the template uses refuses. Use unbind_value on such a line first.

remove_prefab_instance.description: Removes a linked instance: its member sections and its record. Each line outside the instance that names a member stays and shows 'Missing', or goes.

remove_section.description: Removes a section of a mission file. The lines that name it stay and show 'Missing'.

remove_trigger.description: Removes a trigger. Each line that names it stays and shows 'Missing', or goes with references: remove.

rename_item.description: Gives an item a new nickname. With change_references, each line that names it changes too. A ship build of the shared ship build file refuses.

fields.new_name: The new nickname of the item.

rename_prefab_asset.description: Gives a prefab of the active mod a new id, file name and name. Each instance record of the active mod that names it changes too.

fields.new_id: The new id. With the same id, only the name in the library changes.
fields.new_name: The new name in the library. Without it, the name stays.

rename_trigger.description: Gives a trigger a new nickname. With change_references, each line of the script that names the trigger changes too.

fields.new_name: The new nickname of the trigger.

reorder_action.description: Moves an action line of a trigger before another row, or to the end.

fields.row: The action line: an object with its line: reference in ref.
fields.before: The row of the trigger before the move that the action goes before, from 0. Without it, the action goes to the end.

replace_section_body.description: Sets all lines of a section, also the lines before the nickname line. The first nickname cannot change. Use a rename for it.

fields.entries: All lines of the section in order, each with its key and its value texts.

restore_instance_record.description: Puts a record of a linked instance into the graph file of a script. It takes the place of the record with the same id. The inverses use it.

fields.record: The record of the instance, as an inverse gives it.
fields.index: The place of a new record in the list of the records, from 0. Without it, the record goes to the end.

restore_prefab_asset.description: Sets the whole text of a prefab of the active mod, or deletes its file. It does not compile an instance. The inverses use it.

fields.text: The text of the file. Without it, the file goes.

restore_section.description: Puts a section with exact lines at a place of a file. The inverses and the raw INI editor use it.

fields.script: The msn: reference of the script, or of its ship build file.
fields.index: The place of the section in the file, from 0. A larger number puts the section at the end.
fields.section: The section with its type and its lines.

retarget_link.description: Gives a line that names a trigger another trigger. The line is an Act_ActTrig, Act_DeactTrig, Act_Save or Cnd_WatchTrigger line.

fields.row: The line that names a trigger: an object with its line: reference in ref.
fields.target: The nickname of the new trigger in the same script.

revert_override.description: Removes overrides of a linked instance and compiles it. The field takes the value of the prefab again, and a removed member comes back.

fields.field: The field of the override. Without field and member, each override goes.
fields.member: The role of a removed member that comes back.

revert_section.description: Puts back the lines of the base data of a section, or of one key of it. A section that the active mod adds refuses.

fields.name: The key whose lines go back. Without it, the whole section goes back.

set_act.description: Sets the name or the walkthrough text of an act. A field that the command does not give keeps its value.

fields.name: The new name of the act.
fields.text: The new walkthrough text of the act.

set_act_members.description: Sets the triggers of an act in order. A trigger is in one act, so each trigger of the list leaves its other act.

fields.triggers: The nicknames of the triggers of the act, in order.

set_action_line.description: Sets a whole action line, also with a new key.

fields.row: The action line: an object with its line: reference in ref.
fields.line: The new action, with its key and its values by name.

set_action_value.description: Sets one named value of an action line, or a run of values such as a position.

fields.row: The action line: an object with its line: reference in ref.
fields.name: The name of the value, as describe_mission_name gives it.

set_condition.description: Sets the condition of a trigger in the place of the condition that the game uses. A trigger without a condition gets the line after its state lines.

fields.line: The new condition, with its key and its values by name.

set_condition_value.description: Sets one named value of the condition that the game uses for a trigger.

fields.name: The name of the value, as describe_mission_name gives it.

set_formation_members.description: Sets the ship lines of a formation in order. A ship section that comes later in the file moves before the formation, so the game finds the ship.

fields.formation: The sec: reference of the formation.
fields.ships: The nicknames of the ships of the formation, in order.

set_item_key.description: Sets all lines of one key of an item, in their place. A ship key of a ship or a formation goes before the first formation or ship line.

fields.lines: All lines of the key, each with its key and its values by name.

set_line.description: Sets one whole line of a section, also with a new key. The first nickname line cannot change. Use a rename for it.

fields.line: The new line, with its key and its values by name, or its value texts by position in texts.

set_line_text.description: Gives a text id of a line its own text. The text goes into strings.json of the active mod, and the line gets its $str: placeholder.

fields.name: The name of the text id value, as describe_mission_name gives it.

set_line_value.description: Sets one value of a line, by its name or by its index from 0.

fields.name: The name of the value. Without it, index gives the value.
fields.index: The index of the value in the line, from 0, when the command gives no name.

set_orders.description: Sets all order lines of an order list in order. The other lines keep their places.

fields.lines: All order lines in order, each with its key and its values by name.

set_prefab_field.description: Sets a field of a prefab instance. A linked instance gets an override and compiles. A matched instance writes the lines that the field reads.

fields.rows: The rows of the value in their text form, for example 'Cnd_Timer = 5' or my_formation.

set_prefab_field_default.description: Sets the default rows of a field of the template of a prefab, in prefab mode. Each linked instance without an override of the field gets the new value.

fields.rows: The default rows in their text form.

set_prefab_port.description: Sets the outside triggers that a port of a linked instance starts, and compiles the instance.

fields.triggers: The nicknames of the outside triggers that the port starts.

set_ship_loadout.description: Sets the loadout of a mission ship. shared changes the ship build for each ship that uses it. this_ship gives the ship its own copy of the build.

fields.loadout: The nickname of the loadout, for example my_loadout.
fields.scope: shared: change the ship build. this_ship: copy the ship build for this ship only.

set_text.description: Sets a text of the active mod in strings.json, or removes it. The inverse of set_line_text uses it.

fields.key: The key of the text. Use letters, digits, '_', '-' or '.'.
fields.text: The text. Without it, the text goes.

set_trigger_repeats.description: Makes a trigger repeat, or not. True writes repeatable = true at the place of a state line. False removes each repeatable line.

set_trigger_start.description: Makes a trigger start with the mission, or not. True writes InitState = ACTIVE at the place of a state line. False removes the InitState line.

fields.starts: True makes the trigger start with the mission.

set_trigger_system.description: Sets the system line of a trigger. The editor shows it. The game does not read it.

fields.system: The nickname of the system. Without it, the line goes.

unbind_value.description: In prefab mode, makes the slot of a field in a line of the template a fixed value. Without texts, the value takes the default of the field.

fields.value: The name of the value in the line. Without it, the command takes the first slot of the line, or the line of a field.
fields.texts: The fixed value texts. Without them, the value takes the default of the field.

unlink_triggers.description: Removes the lines of a link between two triggers: Act_ActTrig for start, Act_DeactTrig for stop, and both for restart.

fields.source: The trg: reference of the trigger with the action lines.
fields.target: The nickname of the target trigger.
fields.link_kind: The kind of the link: start, stop or restart.

unpack_prefab_instance.description: Removes the record of a linked instance. The member sections stay as plain sections, as Unpack Prefab does in Unity.

RowRef.ref: The line: reference of the line.
RowRef.expect_key: The key that the line must have. Another key refuses with RowChanged.
RowRef.expect_values: The value texts that the line must have. Other values refuse with RowChanged.

GraphPoint.x: The x of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.
GraphPoint.y: The y of the point on the canvas of the mission graph.

NearSpec.anchor: The nickname of the object, for example my_station.
NearSpec.heading: The heading from the object, in degrees.
NearSpec.range: The range from the object, in meters. It is optional.

PilotSpec.faction: The faction of the pilot, for example my_faction.
PilotSpec.head: The head of the pilot in the comm window.
PilotSpec.body: The body of the pilot in the comm window.
PilotSpec.accessories: The accessories of the pilot in the comm window.
PilotSpec.name_text: The text id of the name of the pilot: a number, or $str:<key>.

ShipBuildSpec.archetype: The ship archetype of the build, for example my_ship.
ShipBuildSpec.loadout: The loadout of the build, for example my_loadout.
ShipBuildSpec.pilot: The pilot of the build, for example my_pilot.
ShipBuildSpec.state_graph: The state graph: FIGHTER, TRANSPORT, GUNBOAT, CRUISER, NOTHING or PLAYER.
ShipBuildSpec.level: The level of the build, for example d5.
ShipBuildSpec.npc_classes: The NPC classes of the build.

RawSection.type: The section type, for example MsnShip.
RawSection.entries: The lines of the section in order, each with its key and its value texts.

RawEntry.values: The value texts of the line by position.

NodePlace.x: The x of the node on the canvas of the mission graph.
NodePlace.y: The y of the node on the canvas of the mission graph.
NodePlace.remove: True removes the place, so the graph places the node again.
NodePlace.index: The place of a new record in the list of the node records, from 0. The inverses use it.

PrefabFieldInput.rows: The rows of the value in their text form.

InstancePort.trigger: The nickname of the outside trigger that the port starts.

InstanceRecord.id: The id of the instance in the script.
InstanceRecord.prefab_hash: The hash of the prefab at the last compile.
InstanceRecord.values: The values of the fields that each instance sets itself.
InstanceRecord.overrides: The fields whose value differs from the default of the prefab.
InstanceRecord.removed: The roles of the members that the instance does not have.
InstanceRecord.ports: The outside trigger that each port starts.
InstanceRecord.lines_hash: The hash of the compiled lines. Other lines of the members are a hand edit.

InstanceMember.role: The role of the section in the template of the prefab.
InstanceMember.nickname: The nickname of the section in the script.

InstanceValue.rows: The rows of the value in their text form.

errors.argument_none: The tool {tool} takes no arguments. Remove the argument '{name}'.
errors.argument_unknown: The tool {tool} has no argument '{name}'. Its arguments are: {names}.
errors.argument_missing: The argument '{name}' is necessary. Give it, then call the tool again.
errors.limit_rows: One call can give at most {max} rows. Use a smaller limit and the cursor of the result.
errors.cursor_bad: The cursor is not a cursor of this list. Use the next_cursor of the previous result.
errors.no_profile: No profile is open. Open a profile in the editor, then try again.
errors.limit_calls: The server takes at most {max} calls each second. Wait a moment, then try again.
errors.busy: {reason} The call waited {seconds} seconds. Try again in a few seconds.
errors.limit_tail: The call took more than {seconds} seconds, so the server stopped it.
errors.limit_result: The result has {size} KB of text, and one result can have at most {max} KB. Use a smaller limit, a filter or a tool that reads one item.
errors.editor_only: Only the editor host has the tool {tool}. Start the agent server in the editor.
errors.group_hidden: The user hid the tool group '{group}'. Ask the user to show it in the agent settings.
errors.ref_act: An act: reference names a part of the graph of a mission. Use get_mission for the acts.
errors.ref_cutscene: Use get_cutscene for a whole cutscene. Use get_item for an entity or an event of a cutscene.
errors.ref_or_name: Give a reference or a name, not both.
errors.ref_no_key: The section has no key, so no line can name it.
errors.ref_or_file: Give a reference or a file, not both.
errors.list_unknown: The editor has no data list '{list}'. Use one of these lists: {lists}.
errors.list_needs_system: The list {list} holds the items of one system. Give the argument 'system'.
errors.system_no_file: The system {system} names no system file, so it has no items.
errors.asset_category: The Assets panel has no category '{category}'. Use one of these categories: {categories}.
